event: UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Duncan
venue: Meta APEX, Las Vegas, NV, United States

bouts.title: Brendan Allen vs Christian Leroy Duncan

items.fight_news: Brendan Allen and Christian Leroy Duncan headline the October 10 Fight Night at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Allen enters at 27-7 and Duncan at 15-2, putting two established middleweight contenders in the evening's main event rather than a title fight.

Allen arrives on a three-fight winning streak after defeating Edmen Shahbazyan in June. His recent run also includes victories over Marvin Vettori and Reinier de Ridder, giving him a strong platform to pursue another step toward the middleweight championship picture.

Duncan brings five consecutive wins into the matchup. His last three victories came against Marco Tulio, Roman Dolidze, and Jared Cannonier, making Allen the next substantial test in a run that has moved him into the division's leading contender group.

The main card starts at 8pm Eastern on October 10, following prelims at 5pm Eastern. In India, those starts fall on October 11 at 5:30am and 2:30am respectively. The event streams on Paramount+ in the United States.

Matheus Camilo faces Jai Herbert in the lightweight bout immediately beneath the headliner. Camilo enters at 11-3 and Herbert at 14-6-1, pairing a newer UFC competitor with an opponent who has been part of the promotion since 2020.

Herbert returns after stopping Mandel Nallo in the first round in April. The former Cage Warriors lightweight champion has a recognizable European pedigree, and this assignment gives him an opportunity to extend his recent success against another developing lightweight.

Camilo's UFC record includes a decision victory over Viacheslav Borshchev in November 2025. Facing Herbert on a featured main-card slot offers a different veteran test and a larger platform for a fighter still building his place in the lightweight division.

Loopy Godinez meets Ketlen Souza in a women's strawweight main-card matchup. Godinez enters at 14-6 and holds the No. 8 position, while Souza enters at 17-6. A victory over a ranked opponent would give Souza a meaningful foothold in the division.

Godinez returns after a submission loss to Tatiana Suarez at UFC 327 in April. She previously defeated Jessica Andrade and Julia Polastri, so this booking offers a chance to restart her progress against an opponent outside the current top-ranked group.

Souza comes off a first-round stoppage of Ariane Carnelossi in June, following a decision win over Bruna Brasil in February. Those results give her positive momentum entering a matchup with a more established ranked strawweight on the October 10 main card.

bouts.title: Andre Fili vs Kai Kamaka III

items.fight_news: Andre Fili and Kai Kamaka III meet at featherweight on the main card. Fili enters at 25-14 and Kamaka at 18-8-1, making this one of the card's more experienced pairings rather than a debut or unbeaten-prospect matchup.

Fili has competed in the UFC since 2013 and returns after a June stoppage loss to Vinicius Oliveira. The Kamaka assignment gives the long-serving featherweight a chance to rebuild his momentum against another fighter with extensive professional experience.

Julius Walker faces Gerald Meerschaert at light heavyweight, with Walker entering at 7-3 and Meerschaert at 37-22. The booking brings a veteran best known for his long middleweight career into a matchup with a much less experienced 205-pound opponent.

Walker returns after two stoppage defeats in 2026, most recently against Abdul Rakhman Yakhyaev in June. A win over Meerschaert would help him regain momentum while adding a recognizable veteran name to his developing UFC record.

Malcolm Wellmaker and Otari Tanzilovi meet at bantamweight with matching 10-2 professional records. Their main-card placement gives both fighters a visible opportunity to establish momentum without the immediate stakes of a ranked contender matchup.

Both men are looking to respond to recent UFC setbacks. Wellmaker was submitted by Juan Diaz in May, while Tanzilovi lost a decision to Shane Collins in June. This pairing gives one of them a route back to the win column.

Francisco Prado faces Ismael Bonfim in the lightweight preliminary-card feature. Prado enters at 12-5 and Bonfim at 20-7, giving both fighters a chance to repair recent results in a division where sustained momentum is difficult to build.

Prado has lost four consecutive fights, while Bonfim comes off three consecutive stoppage defeats. The booking therefore carries rebuilding stakes for both men, with a victory offering a practical reset rather than an immediate route into title contention.

Niko Price meets Leon Shahbazyan at welterweight in the prelims. Price enters at 16-11 with two no-contests, while Shahbazyan enters at 12-5. Price's long UFC tenure makes this a recognizable veteran assignment for an opponent early in his promotional run.

Shahbazyan seeks a better second UFC appearance after a first-round stoppage loss to Levan Chokheli in June. Price also arrives after a defeat, having been submitted by Michael Chiesa in March, so both men have an immediate reason to rebuild momentum.

Felipe Franco and Brendson Ribeiro meet in an all-Brazilian light heavyweight preliminary bout. Franco enters at 11-2 and Ribeiro at 17-11 with one no-contest, pairing a newer UFC competitor with an opponent who has accumulated substantially more professional appearances.

Franco earned a second-round stoppage over Levi Rodrigues Jr. in July. Ribeiro lost a decision to Magomed Tuchalov later that month, giving the matchup contrasting recent results: Franco aims to build on a victory while Ribeiro seeks to halt his losing run.

bouts.title: Allen Frye Jr. vs RJ Harris

items.fight_news: Allen Frye Jr. faces RJ Harris at heavyweight in the prelims. Frye enters at 6-1 and Harris at 6-0, with Harris defending an unbeaten professional record against an opponent who has already experienced a full-length UFC contest.

Harris won his UFC debut by stopping Alvin Hines in the first round in July. Frye seeks his first promotional victory after a decision loss to Guilherme Pat in December 2025, giving the matchup clear but different career milestones for each heavyweight.

Alice Pereira meets Daria Zhelezniakova in a women's bantamweight preliminary bout. Pereira enters at 7-1 and Zhelezniakova at 10-3, placing a young Brazilian prospect against a more experienced opponent on the October 10 Las Vegas card.

Pereira earned her first UFC victory by stopping Hailey Cowan in April after losing her debut to Montserrat Rendon. Zhelezniakova returns from a decision defeat to Melissa Croden, so Pereira aims to extend a breakthrough while her opponent seeks a rebound.

Ernesta Kareckaitė and Melissa Gatto open the preliminary card at women's flyweight. Kareckaitė enters at 6-2-1 and Gatto at 9-3-2, giving the October 10 event an experienced international pairing between fighters from Lithuania and Brazil.

Both return after decision defeats earlier this year. Kareckaitė lost to Regina Tarin in February, while Gatto lost a majority decision to Dione Barbosa in April. A win would help either fighter regain momentum before seeking a more prominent divisional assignment.
